name: Levodropropizine

overview.mechanism: Acts as a peripherally acting cough suppressant; the cited clinical trials evaluate symptoms rather than a molecular target [[LEVO-1997,LEVO-2022]].
uses: Studied for symptomatic nonproductive and chronic cough; confirm local indications and age restrictions [[LEVO-1997,LEVO-2022]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Double-blind randomized active-comparator trial; 209 adults; five days.
rows.intervention: Levodropropizine versus dextromethorphan for moderate nonproductive cough.
rows.findings: Both treatments reduced coughing spells; levodropropizine improved nocturnal awakenings more. Reported adverse events were 3.6% versus 12.1%; somnolence 4.6% versus 10.4%.
rows.limitations: No placebo arm and very short follow-up; does not establish long-term or severe-CKD safety.

rows.design: Open-label randomized comparison; 88 participants analyzed; two weeks.
rows.intervention: Levodropropizine versus codeine for chronic cough.
rows.findings: Codeine produced greater improvement in cough severity and quality-of-life measures but more treatment-related adverse events.
rows.limitations: Unblinded active-comparator design; benefit and tolerability cannot be generalized across cough causes or advanced kidney disease.

sources.citation: Efficacy and tolerability of levodropropizine in adult patients with non-productive cough. Comparison with dextromethorphan. PubMed PMID: 9425640.
Effectiveness and Safety of Codeine and Levodropropizine in Patients With Chronic Cough. PubMed PMID: 36123964.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.

common: Somnolence occurred in 4.6% of levodropropizine recipients in the five-day trial. Lower frequency than the comparator does not mean absence of sedation [[LEVO-1997]].

renal: The cited cough trials do not establish a renal adjustment or dialysis schedule. Current product-specific renal restrictions remain to be verified [[LEVO-1997,LEVO-2022]].
